name: Konrad Adenauer
role: First chancellor of West Germany (1949–1963) and CDU leader (1946–1966)
summary: Adenauer, a Catholic Rhinelander, led West Germany for fourteen years on a course of social market economy, firm anti-communism, integration into the West and Europe, and reconciliation with France and Israel. He rejected planned economy, held that parliamentary opposition is a state necessity, and put Western alliance ahead of exploring reunification through neutrality.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He chose competition and the market over planning but warned against rigid doctrine and wanted the state to keep a social role, so agreement is moderate.

traditional-family.rationale: He pledged to stand firmly on Article 6 of the Basic Law putting marriage and family under special state protection against opposing tendencies.

more-religion-public.rationale: He called a return to Europe's Christian roots the surest route to lasting peace and tied the CDU to Christian values.

central-planning.rationale: He told the Bundestag the voters had rejected the planned economy and that Zwangswirtschaft would be abolished wherever possible; the CDU guidelines reject command economy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The CDU guidelines refrain from planning and guiding production, workforce or sales and allow only indirect influence through monetary, tax and trade policy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He said the best life belongs to a people with many middle and small independent livelihoods, and the guidelines aim to turn the poorer classes into property owners.

civilizational-union.rationale: He said Germany belongs to the Western European world and called for a European federation resting on Europe's Christian roots.

conscription.rationale: His government drove the 1954 Basic Law amendment enabling conscription and the 1956 law introducing it.

class-collaboration.rationale: He called a fair balance of social opposites a precondition for the people's rise and said it must be reached by the social partners themselves, not by state tutelage.

population-transfer.rationale: He called the expulsion of Germans contrary to the Potsdam Agreement, and cited Churchill's protest against mass expulsion as a tragedy.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: His government decided in 1951 to ask the Constitutional Court to ban the KPD, which the court did in 1956 for its hostility to the constitutional order.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He cited Article 24 of the Basic Law permitting transfer of sovereign rights and said Germany would gladly join the European Union as a member.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: His government entered the European Defence Community and NATO and he held that a defence alliance with the West was necessary.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: He declined to test the 1952 Soviet offer, yet backed the Western reply demanding free all-German elections, so the record points both ways on reunification.

return-lost-territory.rationale: He said Germany could in no case accept the detachment of the Oder-Neisse territories and would keep pursuing its claim to them by legal means.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: He set the Nazi Gestapo beside its continued use in the Soviet zone and promised vigilance against both right and left radicalism.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: His backing made the Schreiber plan, a pay-as-you-go pension funded from current contributions, the basis of the 1957 reform.

holocaust-denial.rationale: He called the crimes against the Jews unmentionable and demanding moral and material restitution.

social-market-economy.rationale: In the 1949 declaration he named the social market economy over planning as the government's course, with social justice as its guiding star, and the CDU guidelines he chaired set it out as the party programme.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He tied West Germany to the Western bloc, signing the EDC and joining NATO in 1955, and did not take the neutral option offered in 1952.

rent-control.rationale: He planned cautious loosening of rent-fixing and space rationing to bring private capital into housing despite shortage.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: He pushed in 1957 to equip the Bundeswehr with nuclear carrier systems for US-held warheads, despite fierce opposition.

independent-unions.rationale: He declared the government stands on freedom of association and wanted self-administration by the social partners in place of state tutelage.

second-chamber.rationale: He treated the Bundesrat as a partner whose work must be brought into harmony with Bundestag and government, as part of the Basic Law's federal design.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: He created a ministry for Bundesrat affairs to secure the federal character of the Basic Law and safeguard the rights of the Länder.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He held that wages and working conditions are for the social partners to settle, and the guidelines leave them to the collective agreement system.

farm-price-support.rationale: He called for secured production and sales conditions for farm goods at prices covering the costs of average farms.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: He called opposition a state necessity and said progress and habituation to democratic thinking need government and opposition facing each other in parliament.

notes: Sources read: Bundestag plenary record of the 1949 government declaration, GHDI documents (1949-1951 speeches and interviews), the CDU Düsseldorf Guidelines, Bundestag, KAS, bpb and DRV pages on rearmament, the Stalin note, conscription, the KPD ban, pensions and nuclear arms. Themes searched: economy, social policy, Europe and Western alliance, defence, German question, Nazi legacy, party bans, opposition. Federalism and class relations were searched in the 1949 declaration. Courts, executive power, civil liberties, culture and ecology had little stated material in these sources and stay null. The CVCE copy of the 7 February 1952 speech and his memoirs could not be read (CVCE blocked scripted access; memoirs not in any local library).
